## Mandatory context and boundaries
Read the parent epic first. Applicable owners: AGENTS.md; docs/agent-tools.md; docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md; docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md; docs/action-reuse.md; docs/testing-approach.md; docs/services/channels.md (communication/Jido bridge and provider contracts); docs/services/engine.md (history, admission, finalization and delivery). Read docs/documentation.md before documentation/skill edits, docs/services/system-config.md before credential fixtures, and local module @moduledoc before extending a helper. Apply code-quality for code and skill-creator for the skill.
Only test/ additions or backward-compatible support changes, lib/mix/tasks/zaq.test.gen.channel.ex, and .agents/skills/add-channel-integration-tests/** are authorized. Do not edit application modules, dependency source/pins, config, migrations, mix.exs, CI, or unrelated skills. Existing-test expectation changes require the testing handbook's explicit approval; this epic authorizes additive coverage, not changing expectations.
Use real bridges, NodeRouter, Engine admission/history/persistence and configured Agent execution. Only provider/LLM boundaries are faked. A production defect is a reported blocker with a reproducer; do not patch production, silently omit a scenario, weaken an assertion, or close the issue as complete.
Validation timing, failure handling and final gates are owned by docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md. Record executed commands/results in this issue. No new browser E2E is needed: this work adds test/developer infrastructure without changing a deployed UI journey. No commit/push/merge authorization is implied.

Parent epic: zaq-o9d

## Functional specification and files
Own test/zaq/channels/integration/round_trip_test.exs and shared scenario support in case.ex/assertions.ex/contract.ex. At this stage Registry.all/0 must include completed Mattermost, Telegram and WhatsApp drivers. Enumerate this registry in tests; do not hardcode a separate provider list in each scenario file.
Create distinct ExUnit test names and provider/scenario tags. All common runtime cases are enabled by default, async: false, without :integration exclusions. Every implemented registry entry participates automatically. An incomplete registered scaffold must fail with provider/callback detail, never skip.
Required scenarios per provider:
1. Direct Hello -> observed real LLM request containing that exact user text -> deterministic Hello answer -> correct native recipient; final visible content after any status creation/edit.
2. Shared room message with actual provider mention -> model input -> correct room reply.
3. Same scenario with persisted mention_required and unmentioned message -> factual capture, no model request or answer, after completed-ingress barrier.
4. Two sequential messages in one session -> second model request contains only the permitted first exchange plus new input; explicitly wait for actual runtime terminal readiness before next input.
5. Replay identical native input -> one admitted execution/canonical user input/final answer (status traffic is not counted as another answer).
6. At least one representative real registered tool invocation using ToolCallingLLMStub, with independently expected tool result and final answer. Keep basic per-provider scenarios tool-free; do not force tools merely to satisfy mocks.
Use plain deterministic text for baseline cross-provider assertions; provider formatting is tested separately. Keep exact native source ids and output correlation visible in test bodies.

## Tests to add before implementation
These scenarios are the tests: author failing expectations first, then only improve test harness/provider mechanics until they run. Add a meta/regression check that a newly registered synthetic driver fixture is enumerated by all shared scenario registries, and that missing required callbacks fail rather than produce zero tests.
Where a real product bug is exposed, preserve its reproducer and record a blocker; do not alter production or relax expectations. Deliberate provider differences are explicit optional scenarios, not disabled baseline direct/shared cases.

## Branches/paths validated
Direct/shared/passive, one/two turns, duplicate/replay, tool-free/tool execution, create/edit status lifecycle and all-provider enumeration.

## Mocking plan
External provider plus LLM only. The shared suite enters at native adapter ingress and proves actual Agent/Engine execution. Do not count a fabricated callback observation as the complete round trip.

## Documentation
Add a copyable minimal scenario and full-matrix versus provider-targeted commands to README; document that all-driver validation is required before declaring any new adapter integration complete.

## Action reuse assessment
Reuse existing native provider drivers, LLM mocks, Case lifecycle and real runtime dispatch/operations. Common scenario functions are local-only test composition with assertions, not duplicate routing or business Actions. Verification is native ingress -> observed LLM -> provider receipt -> actual completion.

## Done when
All baseline scenarios pass for the three providers, registry growth expands the matrix automatically, no scenario is hidden by default tags, and one real tool execution is proven.

comments.text: Implemented Registry.all-driven direct/shared, observed LLM/native-recipient, passive mention-required capture, two sequential turns, native replay and one actual arithmetic.add tool execution. Added completion barrier on actual HistorySync.complete return, correlated to persisted input, before starting another turn. Shared matrix first run: 34 tests passed; complete implemented suite: 80 tests + 2 properties with only independently tracked Telegram policy/dedupe/thread defects, no baseline round-trip failures. mix q passes. All common cases enabled by default; no provider allowlist.
